subtype: Managing Anger, Envy & Ego at Work
passage: At the cooperative sugar factory near Kolhapur, Pradeep had trained Indu when she joined. Two years later she was made shift supervisor, not him. He heard it at the tea stall and felt his face burn. That evening he snapped at his younger brother over nothing. At night he lay awake, thinking of every mistake she'd ever made. The next morning he nearly skipped her first meeting. Instead he went, sat at the back and said little. Afterward he walked by the cane fields and admitted to himself that she was good at planning, better than him. He congratulated her the next day, stiffly. She said, "You taught me half of it." His chest loosened a little.

qa.q: Where did Pradeep hear about Indu's promotion?
qa.a: He heard it at the tea stall.

qa.q: What does Pradeep lying awake thinking of Indu's mistakes suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he felt envious and hurt, looking for reasons she didn't deserve the promotion.

qa.q: How did Pradeep manage his envy professionally?
qa.a: He attended her meeting, reflected honestly on her strengths and congratulated her, even if stiffly.

qa.q: How might Indu have seen Pradeep's congratulations?
qa.a: She probably noticed the stiffness but valued it, and her reply showed she respected him.

grounding: Shows a young man handling envy and hurt pride after a colleague's promotion in a professional way.

subtype: Managing Anger, Envy & Ego at Work
passage: Rosa had worked at the Lima architecture firm longer than Bao, but it was Bao's design the partners chose for the library project. In the meeting, Rosa smiled and clapped. In the bathroom afterward, she gripped the sink and breathed. She wanted to point out, loudly, that his design ignored drainage. Instead, she waited until the next morning, calmer. She wrote Bao a short message: "Congrats. One thing to check, the drainage on the east side might flood in heavy rain. Happy to help." Bao replied, "You're right, I missed that. Can we look together?" They spent an afternoon on it. Rosa still felt a pinch when the partners praised him. But the building would be better.

qa.q: Which project did the partners choose Bao's design for?
qa.a: They chose it for the library project.

qa.q: What was Rosa feeling when she gripped the sink?
qa.a: She felt envious and angry, and was trying to calm herself before reacting.

qa.q: What made Rosa's handling of her feelings professional?
qa.a: She waited until she was calm and raised a real problem helpfully instead of attacking Bao in front of others.

qa.q: How might Bao see Rosa after her message?
qa.a: He probably sees her as generous and skilled, since he welcomed her help.

grounding: Shows a young architect managing envy and ego after a rival's success by acting professionally.

subtype: Managing Anger, Envy & Ego at Work
passage: In the break room of the city hospital's billing department, Nazia heard a colleague say that Rekha, the new manager, had been hired because she was the director's niece. Nazia had applied for the same job. Her ears went hot. For days she was curt with Rekha and rolled her eyes in meetings. Then Rekha asked to speak with her privately. "I know you wanted this role," Rekha said. "I'd value your experience. Can you lead the new system training?" Nazia wanted to stay angry. Instead she said, "Okay. And I'm sorry I've been rude." She never found out if the rumour was true. She decided to judge Rekha by her work instead.

qa.q: Where did Nazia hear the rumour about Rekha?
qa.a: She heard it in the break room of the billing department.

qa.q: Why was Nazia curt with Rekha for days?
qa.a: She was envious and hurt about missing the job, and the rumour fed her anger.

qa.q: What helped Nazia move past her anger?
qa.a: Rekha's respectful offer gave her a real role, and Nazia chose to apologise and judge Rekha by her work.

qa.q: How might Rekha have felt about Nazia's eye-rolling?
qa.a: She likely noticed and felt the tension, but chose to address it privately and with respect.

grounding: Shows a young worker moving from envy and rivalry to professional conduct after missing a promotion.

subtype: Managing Anger, Envy & Ego at Work
passage:
Hi Karthik,
I owe you an apology for Thursday's meeting. When your promotion was announced, I congratulated you in two words and then shot down your first proposal harder than it deserved. That wasn't about the proposal. Honestly, I was envious. We joined in the same month, and I'd been telling myself the role was mine. I went home angry, mostly at myself. I've thought about it since. You led the vendor migration when no one else wanted it, and you did it well. I can learn from that. I'd still like to discuss my concerns about the budget line, calmly this time, maybe on Monday? And I'll say it properly now: congratulations. You earned it.
Asif

qa.q: What did Asif do in Thursday's meeting?
qa.a: Asif gave a two-word congratulation and then criticised Karthik's first proposal harder than it deserved.

qa.q: What feeling was really behind Asif's harsh criticism?
qa.a: Envy; they joined in the same month and Asif had privately counted on getting the role.

qa.q: What makes Asif's email a good repair?
qa.a: Asif names the behaviour and its real cause honestly, recognises Karthik's merit, and offers to raise genuine concerns calmly.

qa.q: How might Karthik feel after reading the email?
qa.a: Relieved and respected, and more open to hearing Asif's budget concerns now that the tension is explained 🙂

grounding: An email shows a young professional owning their envy after a colleague's promotion and repairing the relationship.

subtype: Managing Anger, Envy & Ego at Work
passage: Jeevan, you asked about my worst ego moment at work. Easy. Last year, on a client call, our intern, just twenty-one, interrupted me: 'Sorry, Anirban sir, that figure is wrong.' In front of the client. I felt heat go up my neck. I actually opened my mouth to say, 'Let's take that offline,' which would have meant: be quiet. Then I looked at the sheet. She was right. So I said, 'Good catch, thank you; the correct number is what she said.' The client smiled. After the call I walked around the block because I was still angry, and not really at her. At myself for being wrong, and at the feeling of being shown up. When I came back I told her the catch was great, and that next time she could message me privately first. She did, from then on.

qa.q: What did the intern point out during the client call?
qa.a: That Anirban's figure was wrong.

qa.q: What did the heat going up Anirban's neck show about how he felt?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed and threatened, his ego stung at being corrected in front of a client.

qa.q: What did Anirban do that kept things professional?
qa.a: He checked the sheet, thanked her publicly, cooled off with a walk, and later gave her private guidance on how to raise such issues.

qa.q: How might the intern have felt when Anirban thanked her?
qa.a: Relieved and respected, since she had taken a risk correcting a senior in front of a client.

grounding: A young professional describes managing a flash of anger and wounded ego when a junior corrected him in public.
